question: Why are certain cognitions in those oriented toward isolation not products of past habit?
premises: Some cognitions arise in those oriented toward isolation.
These cognitions were never practiced before.
Given the nature of transmigration, they cannot be explained by prior habituation.
inference: Such unprecedented cognitions must be attributed to the descent of power rather than to worldly habit.
uncertainties: saṃsṛterbhāvāt is brief; it likely means that transmigratory habit would have produced prior familiarity if that were the cause.
plain_english: In those oriented toward isolation, some cognitions arise that were never practiced before. Because of the nature of transmigration, these cannot come from habit and must come from the descent of power.
